summary: This article explains what black holes are, how they form when giant stars collapse, and how scientists find and even photograph something that gives off no light.
introduce: Show the three key terms on the board and ask students to rate each one: “I know it,” “I have seen it,” or “It is new.” Tell them to watch for these words in “Black Holes” and use clues around them to understand their meaning.

keyTerms.def: to fall down or fall inward suddenly
an edge or line you cannot see past

challengeTerms.def: a giant explosion that happens when a very large star dies
having a lot of matter packed tightly into a small space
extremely large in mass, millions or billions of times more than the Sun

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that black holes are the most interesting things in space? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Describe, step by step, how a massive star becomes a black hole.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review massive, collapse, and horizon, and let weak readers draw a quick picture for each term and use it in a short spoken sentence.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use supernova, dense, and supermassive in a short paragraph that teaches the class one of the terms with their own example.
